hints.title: Turn the drawing into coordinate rules
hints.body: A point lies on a drawn segment only when it has the segment’s fixed coordinate and its other coordinate lies between the endpoints. Read the successive corner coordinates before extrapolating.
hints.recap: Fixed coordinate plus endpoint range decides membership.
hints.pitfall: An expanding spiral is not a collection of complete closed squares.
hints.pause: List the corners from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> through the displayed outer loop.

hints.title: Compare the two vertical sides
hints.body: At x=2, the vertical segment runs from y=−2 to y=2. At x=−2, it runs only from y=−2 to y=0. The next left side x=−4 ends at y=2, while the right side x=4 reaches y=4.
hints.recap: The left side stops two units below the matching top height.
hints.pitfall: The spiral continues outwards before closing that apparent corner.
hints.pause: Write the upper and lower y-values on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: A pattern needs the rule that repeats it; inspect the whole state rather than a few matching values.

hints.title: Apply the segment ranges
hints.body: Use your general endpoint rules at the even coordinates in the options. Check whether each proposed point lies within its corresponding vertical or horizontal segment.
hints.recap: The segment’s fixed coordinate and the other coordinate’s range must both match.
hints.pitfall: A point absent from one segment can only be rescued by a different segment that actually passes through it.
hints.pause: Evaluate the listed points and identify the one absent from the entire spiral.

recall.reminder: The segment’s fixed coordinate and the other coordinate’s range must both match.

solution:
The displayed corners begin (0,0), (−2,0), (−2,−2), (2,−2), (2,2), (−4,2), (−4,−4), (4,−4), (4,4). Each new pair of turns extends the square pattern by two units.

For a positive integer k, the right vertical side x=2k covers −2k≤y≤2k. The left vertical side x=−2k covers −2k≤y≤2k−2. The top side y=2k covers −2k−2≤x≤2k, and the bottom side y=−2k covers −2k≤x≤2k.

Thus y=100 and y=−100 both contain the listed x-values ±99. The side x=100 contains y=±99. The side x=−100 contains y=−99 but stops at y=98, so it does not contain (−100,99). No horizontal segment has odd y-coordinate 99.

Answer G: (−100,99).
knowledgePattern: Extend the square spiral using its even-coordinate boundaries
